Subject: MAP request: pilot legal sequencing + MSA/DPA/order form dependencies

Hi Soojin —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and procurement teams asked for a short Mutual Action Plan so we can map dependencies between the MSA, DPA, and order form and land the pilot start date. High level asks from my side:

- Can Redwood sign the MSA before we execute the order form, or do you require the order form first for billing?
- What evidence (SOC2, network diagram, KMS attestation) do you need before we can go live?
- Can you provide suggested milestone owners and target dates (legal review, security sign-off, PO issuance, order form signature, billing start)?

I've attached a rough MAP from our side (MediBridge-MAP-draft.xlsx) — it's a starting point. Procurement are asking for a one-page timeline they can share with the CFO.

We'd like to target a pilot kickoff week of July 7–11 if possible. If any of the legal items push past that, what's your contingency (staged access, trial credits, or scoped early access)?

Appreciate your help — copying our procurement inbox.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Director, Partnerships | MediBridge
liam.oconnor@medibridge.com

Subject: Re: MAP request: pilot legal sequencing + MSA/DPA/order form dependencies

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the clear ask and the draft MAP — very helpful. Quick answers up front:

- Redwood prefers the MSA in place before a paid order form goes live, but for pilots we're flexible: we can accept a signed order form to enable billing while the MSA/DPA finish negotiation, provided we put in a short-term staging clause (30-day contingency) that pauses billing if legal roadblocks appear.
- Minimum evidence to start a pilot with production-like data: current SOC 2 Type II report, a high-level network diagram, and confirmation of encryption-at-rest (KMS) approach. If you need to share anonymized datasets we can relax some requirements temporarily.
- I'll propose a MAP with owners and dates below and loop in Legal (Karthik) and Ops (Laura) for any hard constraints.

Proposed condensed MAP (week-by-week targets):
- Week 1 (Jun 16–20): Shared MAP + security evidence exchange — owner: MediBridge procurement (Liam).
- Week 2 (Jun 23–27): Redwood initial review (legal redlines flagged) — owner: Karthik Iyer (Legal).
- Week 3 (Jun 30–Jul 4): Finalize DPA + minor MSA redlines — owner: Legal / Liam to resolve procurement items.
- Week 4 (Jul 7–11): Order form signature & pilot kickoff (soft start) — owner: Liam / Laura Bennett (CS Ops)

Fallbacks and contingency:
- If MSA/DPA not ready by Week 4, we can do a scoped technical onboarding (read-only API keys + sandbox quotas) with a temporary evaluation credit for up to two weeks.
- For billing: we can hold billing until the order form is signed; alternatively start billing upon order form and retro-rate if the MSA requires adjustments.

Next steps I propose:
1) I will draft a compact MAP spreadsheet with milestones and owners and share by end of day today (RDW-proposed-MAP-v1.xlsx).
2) Karthik — can Legal confirm whether the proposed contingency (30-day staging clause) is acceptable or if Legal insists on full MSA before order form?
3) Liam — please confirm target pilot week and attach SOC2 + network diagram when available.

Would you be available for a 20‑minute alignment call today or tomorrow to lock dates?

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Subject: Re: MAP request: pilot legal sequencing + MSA/DPA/order form dependencies

Liam / Soojin —

Quick legal note on sequencing and a couple of hard stops we need to highlight:

1) Sequence preference: MSA signature before order form is our standard. For pilots we can accept an order form provided that:
   - The order form explicitly references the pending MSA version and includes an automatic fallback to the MSA terms once executed.
   - The order form contains an explicit termination / pause clause tied to unresolved legal obligations (data residency, export controls).

2) DPA: must be executed either as an exhibit to the MSA or as a standalone DPA signed by both parties prior to any PHI-level processing. If MediBridge intends to send PHI, we need the executed DPA in place.

3) Evidence: SOC 2 Type II (latest), KMS provider name and key management outline, and a brief network diagram (redacted IPs OK). We also need the primary contact for security assessments.

4) Typical turnaround: If we receive a clean MSA with only standard redlines, Legal can turn in 3–5 business days. Complex redlines or procurement-mandated addenda can add 1–2 weeks.

5) DocuSign / signatures: please use the powerform link below when ready. If procurement requires a PO, we can accept a signed PO and pair it with the order form.

DocuSign link (powerform): https://docusign.com/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abc-123-def

I'll review RDW-proposed-MAP-v1 and post comments inline by EOD. If we need a tighter timeline, I can do a short legal sprint with a single redline pass.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal Operations | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
